title: Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centers: unified management of Teams apps and agents across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app
summary: The rollout account and the listed paths and commands are supported. The briefing nevertheless says its sources do not cover Microsoft 365 admin center permissions, although its cited cross-application app guide explicitly restricts those controls to Global Administrators. State that documented requirement and keep only the narrower question about role interactions after unification open.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Unified management lets administrators manage cross-host Teams apps and agents from either admin center across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app.
claims.quote: Ensures org-wide defaults for both admin centers are in sync and governs app availability across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft Copilot apps

claims.claim: The roadmap says Integrated Apps changes previously affected these apps only on Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App.
claims.quote: Before this update, changes made through the Integrated Apps section in the Microsoft 365 admin center would only affect these apps on Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App

claims.claim: The roadmap says Teams admin center changes previously affected only Teams.
claims.quote: similarly, changes made in the Teams admin center would exclusively affect Teams.

claims.claim: After unification, org-wide setting changes synchronize automatically between the two centers in both directions.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.claim: After unification, app status changes synchronize automatically between the two centers.
claims.quote: After unification, changes made to the app status, org-wide settings, and user assignment in either admin center are synchronized in the other.

claims.claim: After unification, app availability and user assignment changes synchronize between the two centers.

claims.where: What's changing: comparison of the two Learn guides
claims.claim: The cross-application app guide still describes separate Teams settings, whereas the unified-management guide describes synchronization after unification.
claims.quote: Any changes made on the integrated apps portal on the Microsoft 365 admin center only impact whether and how a cross application app is surfaced on Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application. To manage how these apps show up on Teams, use the Teams admin center.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The default is on in the sense that never-modified tenants unify automatically without administrator action.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: Modified tenants can choose to unify using Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Select **Move to unified app management**. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: For differing settings, the wizard lets administrators select which center's org-wide and app-level settings to apply.
claims.quote: Select the admin center’s settings that you want to apply from the **Apply settings from** drop-down list and select **Apply settings**.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Only a Global admin can consent to unification and apply the final changes.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Any Teams or Global admin can prepare updates through Review summary.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the **Review summary** page.

claims.claim: MC796790 includes a text update dated 18 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Phase 1 targets never-modified tenants and began rolling out at the end of September 2025.
claims.quote: We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock

claims.claim: Phase 2 for modified tenants is described as fully rolled out.
claims.quote: This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: In Phase 2, org-wide and app-level settings do not change without administrator action.
claims.quote: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Phase 3 will automatically unify availability for tenants that have not acted.
claims.quote: Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase.

claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The supplied notice does not yet announce a Phase 3 start date.
claims.quote: The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.

claims.claim: Unified installation management is generally available.
claims.quote: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Installation unification applies to tenants whose availability has been unified.
claims.quote: Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible.

claims.claim: Installations unify across the centers within 24 to 48 hours after completing availability unification.
claims.quote: app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Supported app and agent installation assignments synchronize across the two centers.
claims.quote: Existing installation assignments for supported apps and agents will be synchronized across both admin centers.

claims.claim: MC796790 associates roadmap items 393931, 485712 and 503105.
claims.quote: This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises keeping settings synchronized manually until the tenant migrates to unified management.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized.

claims.claim: The Microsoft pages describe settings synchronization rather than new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management approval data. Read uam-tac-mac, manage-apps and supplied MC796790; none describes new data access granted by unification itself.

claims.claim: The unified-management page describes no approval step for each subsequent synchronized change.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management approval data. Read uam-tac-mac: consent is documented for moving to the unified state, and subsequent synchronization is automatic; no per-change approval is documented.

claims.quote: Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Teams admin center management page names Teams Administrator as the required role.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A licensing entitlement specifically covering unified agent and app management is not published, so the model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: uam-tac-mac licensing requirements unified app management Teams; unified app management license. Read uam-tac-mac, manage-apps, using-admin-roles and Teams service description; no unification entitlement is stated.

claims.claim: The sources publish no meter for unified management itself.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management license licensing pricing meter; uam-tac-mac licensing requirements unified app management Teams. Read uam-tac-mac, manage-apps and Teams service description; none states a meter for unification.

claims.claim: The two named management guides do not name a license prerequisite for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: uam-tac-mac licensing requirements unified app management Teams. Read uam-tac-mac and manage-apps in full: the latter names Teams Administrator, but neither states a license prerequisite for unification.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: third-party app fees
claims.claim: Individual third-party apps can have their own publisher-provided paid subscriptions or licenses.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/purchase-third-party-apps to sources for the sentence about separate third-party app licenses and fees.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, export the app catalogue
claims.claim: Administrators can export the app catalog from the Teams admin center to review status and availability.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center. It can help you to coordinate with admin and security teams to evaluate agents and apps, verify availability, verify status, and more.

claims.claim: The alignment wizard supports resolving multiple apps together by choosing a center's settings.
claims.quote: Bulk app resolution: Select multiple apps at a time and select either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center from the **Apply settings from** drop-down list.

claims.claim: The unification entry point is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Go to **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**. The **Manage apps** page appears. ... Select **Move to unified app management**. The **Align org-wide app settings** page appears.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for the move to unified management itself is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams unified app management migration PowerShell Microsoft Graph unification state; unified app management API. Read uam-tac-mac and Update-M365TeamsApp; results document UI migration and app assignments, not a scripted unification operation.

claims.claim: The allow/block control is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**. ... Select the app on the **Manage apps** page and select **Allow** or **Block** option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -IsBlocked $true is a documented MicrosoftTeams command for changing app state.
claims.quote: PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: App availability is reached through Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability.
claims.quote: Select the **Users and groups** tab. ... Under **Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization**, select **Availability**. ... Select **Edit availability**.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp supports selecting an app and adding group assignments with -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group IDs>.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: Teams admin center does not support bulk availability updates, but PowerShell does.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.claim: The custom-app switch is under Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Custom apps > Let users install and use available apps by default.
claims.quote: On **Manage apps** page, under the **Actions** menu, select **Org-wide app settings**. ... Under **Custom apps**, turn off or turn on **Let users install and use available apps by default** option.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp -isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled $True sets the Custom Apps switch.
claims.quote: There is a switch for managing Custom Apps in the Org-wide App Settings page of Teams Admin Center. The command can set the value of this switch. If the isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled is set to true, the switch is enabled.

claims.claim: The custom-app cmdlet concerns the Custom Apps switch, including custom package upload and availability, rather than the Microsoft apps or third-party apps switches.
claims.quote: The value to Custom Apps Setting. If the value is true, the custom apps can be uploaded as app packages and available in the organization's app store, vice versa.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 availability path is Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install.
claims.quote: Scroll down and select **Edit Users** or select the **Users** tab in the overview pane. ... **Specific users/group in the organization can install** means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center's Integrated apps availability interface has no separately documented direct automation operation.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph integrated apps app availability admin center users groups API; Integrated apps availability PowerShell. Read cross-application app guide, uam-tac-mac and Update-M365TeamsApp; no separate Integrated apps availability call found.

claims.where: Governance controls: qualification of the Teams cmdlets
claims.claim: The cited PowerShell reference does not explain how individual calls appear in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams unified app management migration PowerShell Microsoft Graph unification state. Read Update-M365TeamsApp and Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp references and uam-tac-mac; synchronization is described generally, not as MAC results for each call.

claims.where: Open questions: Microsoft 365 admin center roles
claims.claim: The pages read do not cover which Microsoft 365 admin center roles can change availability on Integrated apps.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins. Check your credentials before you proceed.
claims.fix: Replace the roles bullet in Open questions with: "The cited cross-application app guide says its Integrated apps controls are available only to Global Admins. It does not explain how those permissions interact with the Teams Administrator role after unification."

claims.claim: Teams apps can be enhanced to work in Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App.
claims.quote: App developers can enhance their Microsoft Teams apps to work in Outlook and in Microsoft 365 App (formerly known as Office.com).
